content_units: Starter Anime for a 13-Year-Old

These six series are good entry points for a younger teen: age-appropriate, not overly violent, and all comfortably under 80 episodes. The order below goes from easiest to jump into toward shows with a bit more emotional nuance and thematic depth.
Recommended Watch Order
Order   Series   Genre   Episodes   Why it fits
1    Haikyu!!    Sports / Comedy / Team drama   25   Instantly likable, energetic, and very easy to follow
2    Spy x Family    Comedy / Action / Family   37+   Funny, stylish, and broadly appealing without being heavy
3    K-On!    Slice of life / Music / Comedy   39   Warm, relaxing, and character-driven
4    Little Witch Academia    Fantasy / School / Adventure   25   Magical and upbeat, with a bit more story momentum
5    Mob Psycho 100    Supernatural / Comedy / Coming-of-age   37   Deeper emotions and growth, but still very accessible
6    A Place Further than the Universe    Adventure / Friendship / Drama   13   The most emotionally resonant of the group
Six Strong Starter Picks
Option 1:  Haikyu!!    High-energy sports anime with heart   Best for instant hook

If your cousin has never watched anime before,  Haikyu!!  is probably the easiest win. It follows a short but fiercely determined volleyball player who joins a team and learns how much effort, trust, and teamwork matter. It’s exciting without being violent, funny without being silly all the time, and full of characters who are easy to root for. Even people who do not care about sports often end up loving it because the real appeal is the friendships, rivalries, and constant underdog energy.
Option 2:  Spy x Family    Comedy-action with a fake family twist   Best all-around crowd-pleaser

Spy x Family  is a very safe and fun recommendation for a 13-year-old because it mixes action, comedy, and wholesome family moments in a way that feels light rather than intense. A master spy builds a fake family for a mission, not realizing his new “wife” is an assassin and his adopted daughter is secretly a telepath. The action is stylized rather than harsh, and the real charm comes from watching these three odd people slowly become a real family. It has broad humor, memorable characters, and a fast pace that makes it easy for a beginner to stick with.
Option 3:  K-On!    Cozy school comedy about starting a band   Best for a relaxed vibe

If your cousin likes chill, funny, low-stress stories,  K-On!  is a great pick. It’s about a group of girls who join their school’s light music club and spend as much time hanging out, joking around, and drinking tea as they do practicing. There is very little conflict, almost no real danger, and the whole show is built around friendship and everyday fun. It’s a strong starter because it shows a side of anime that is comforting and character-focused rather than action-heavy.
Option 4:  Little Witch Academia    Bright magical-school adventure   Best for fantasy fans

Little Witch Academia  feels like a cheerful gateway into fantasy anime. It follows Akko, an enthusiastic but not naturally gifted girl who enrolls in a witch academy because she was inspired by a stage magician. The show has colorful magic, school rivalry, adventure, and lots of uplifting energy, but it stays friendly and age-appropriate. It is especially good for someone who likes imaginative worlds, expressive animation, and stories about determination mattering more than talent.
Option 5:  Mob Psycho 100    Supernatural comedy with real emotional growth   Best for character development

Mob Psycho 100  is one of the best beginner anime once someone is ready for a little more emotional depth. It follows a quiet middle-school boy with overwhelming psychic powers who is trying to become a better, more confident person rather than just a stronger one. There are action scenes, but the tone is more strange, funny, and heartfelt than brutal. What makes it stand out is how kind its message is: self-worth does not come from power, popularity, or talent alone, and growing as a person matters most.
Option 6:  A Place Further than the Universe    Adventure drama about friendship and courage   Best for emotional impact

This is the most emotionally complex recommendation here, but still very appropriate for a young teen.  A Place Further than the Universe  follows four girls who join an expedition to Antarctica, each carrying her own reasons for going. It starts as a friendship adventure and gradually becomes a moving story about regret, courage, ambition, and stepping into a bigger world. There is no heavy violence, and the series is short, focused, and very rewarding. It’s a great pick once your cousin is ready for anime that hits a little deeper emotionally without becoming too dark.
Quick Start Picks
- If they want something exciting right away: start with  Haikyu!!
- If they want comedy first: start with  Spy x Family
- If they like fantasy: start with  Little Witch Academia
- If they prefer emotional stories: build up to  A Place Further than the Universe
Helpful Viewing Notes

A few popular anime are often recommended to beginners but are less ideal for this specific request because they can be longer, darker, or more violent. These six avoid that problem while still giving a nice mix of sports, comedy, slice-of-life, fantasy, supernatural, and drama.
